newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac rises on Wallis inquiry talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac rises on Wallis inquiry talk.

text.p: Shares in Westpac Banking Corp soared on Friday on speculation that Treasurer Peter Costello had received the recommendations of the Wallis Inquiry and that it would be released to the market today or early next week.
At 3.10 p.m. (0410 GMT), Westpac shares were 32 cents up to A$7.38 with over 2.2 million shares traded.
"I believe the Treasurer has already received the recommendation in the Wallis Inquiry, so he may release something on that today or early next week," one Melbourne-based broker said.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) shares were also stronger. At 3.10 p.m. (0410 GMT), ANZ shares were 20 cents or 2.54 percent up to A$8.07.
"People will be watching those (Westpac and ANZ) stocks as they are the target stocks," the broker said.
A spokeswoman for the Treasurer told Reuters this morning that Costello had not received the Wallis report yet.
"The market thinks they have, whether the market is right or wrong time will tell," the broker said.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia was the other of Australia's big four banks to rise. At 3.20 (0420 GMT), Commonwealth shares were 11 cents up at A$12.59.
While National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) was four cents weaker at A$15.56. NAB is seen by the market as a predator in any loosening of Australia's banking ownership laws.
